scientific_question: At what phase and spatial/temporal scale is capture-time Durif readiness transferable as a predictor of European eel migration?
priority_design: phase-resolved activation/onset versus post-activation progression using independently measured capture-time Durif stage

primary_cohort.rule: metadata-only individuals absent from processed migration tables are not classified as biological non-migrants

endpoints: time to threshold-defined first downstream-migration crossing

gate2_primary_progression.endpoint: source-defined post-activation whole-migration speed among expert-corrected initiators in informative project-year strata
gate2_primary_progression.estimand: multiplicative speed ratio per ordinal Durif stage
gate2_primary_progression.interpretation: Among eels that crossed the stage-dependent activation gate, no transferable general Durif-stage speed ranking is detected. This is a selected post-activation population and not a causal estimate of stage attenuation in all tagged eels.

secondary_terminal_endpoint_sensitivity.endpoint: membership in the source study's project-specific terminal positive set among activated eels
secondary_terminal_endpoint_sensitivity.boundary: Non-membership is not a validated biological failure state; terminal-set analyses and the former stacked phase OR contrast are sensitivity analyses only.

external_boundary.implication: Silvering stage can contribute to finer reach-level progression, so post-activation state effects are phase-, scale- and context-dependent rather than universally absent.

evidence_boundary: The Europe-wide results support a transferability boundary in capture-stage information, not a causal proof that internal-state effects weaken after activation. Post-activation speed conditions on a stage-dependent entry filter. River Test is an external scale boundary, Dutch is a confounded event-level mechanism candidate requiring arrival-defined risk sets, and Lithuania is a route-bottleneck contrast.

river_test.design_strength: all tagged eels released together after capture during an active downstream migration period
river_test.result: silvering stage was retained in a reach-level progression-rate model together with temperature, barriers, flow and moon illumination
river_test.interpretation: post-activation readiness information can remain detectable at finer spatial scale even when the six-project whole-route speed effect is near zero
river_test.not_claimed: formal replication of the Europe-wide phase model

dutch_pump_tidal_sluice.risk_set: arrival-defined discharge events after first direct barrier detection and before confirmed downstream passage
known_design_boundaries: source-defined opportunity eligibility itself uses discharge duration and therefore cannot be the primary risk set for a duration mechanism test
9 of 11 FIII fish were in the first release cohort whereas FIV/FV were spread across all three releases
Durif stage and body mass were non-identifiable at the tidal sluice in the source study
dutch_pump_tidal_sluice.not_claimed: clean independent confirmation of a general internal-to-external control handoff

lithuania_river_lagoon.source: Dainys et al. 2026 Estuarine Coastal and Shelf Science
lithuania_river_lagoon.result: published migration success is high through free-flowing rivers but declines during subsequent Curonian Lagoon progression
lithuania_river_lagoon.interpretation: post-activation limitation can move downstream from river passage to a later route compartment
lithuania_river_lagoon.not_claimed: readiness-stage replication unless individual stage variation and data access are verified

project_and_scale_heterogeneity.conclusion: No hidden transferable general stage gradient detected across project or the frozen median positive inter-station speed summary.

capture_stage_staleness.boundary: No repeated post-release Durif measurements; physiological convergence is not falsified.

activation_filter_selection.boundary: Activation is a stage-dependent selected principal stratum. Measured-predictor weighting does not restore a general gradient, but latent readiness selection remains unidentifiable.

activation_gate_body_state.interpretation: Capture weight-for-length state retains additive predictive information for whether and when classified migration activates beyond the ordinal Durif label.
activation_gate_body_state.boundary: Durif classification itself uses body morphometrics including length and weight, so this is continuous biometric information beyond an ordinal stage label, not an independent energetic or physiological axis and not a causal mechanism.

pattern: Europe-wide: better capture body state predicts higher activation probability and earlier onset beyond ordinal Durif stage.
Huisman et al. 2023 tidal sluice: higher weight/condition predicts more missed sluicing events before passage.
van Rijn et al. 2026 pumping station: better condition predicts more missed passage opportunities before passage.
van der Knaap et al. 2025 pumping station: higher condition predicts lower routine acceleration.
condition_phase_reversal_hypothesis.candidate_mechanism: After promoting entry into migration, high body state may increase selectivity for stronger/safer passage opportunities at engineered barriers, consistent with state-dependent stimulus thresholds or asset protection.
condition_phase_reversal_hypothesis.decisive_test: arrival-defined Dutch barrier risk sets linking observed barrier arrival to discharge events, then test body condition x opportunity strength while retaining release-group and stage/body-mass confounding checks
condition_phase_reversal_hypothesis.evidence_boundary: The elapsed-time decomposition is same-cohort but post hoc and conditions on activation. Elapsed time is not a direct stop-duration measure. External Dutch studies provide a candidate passage-delay mechanism, not causal confirmation.

frozen_positive_interstation_speed.interpretation: no negative active-transit-speed gradient; leave-one-project-out signs are not uniformly negative

whole_route_decomposition.interpretation: the negative whole-route-speed point estimate is carried mainly by longer elapsed migration time rather than slower positive inter-station transit

condition_phase_reversal_hypothesis.revised_candidate_mechanism: Do not assign the Europe-wide elapsed-time tendency to general condition-dependent barrier selectivity. Retain the broader phase-transferability result: capture-state information strongly predicts entry/onset but is weak as a transferable general post-activation progression-speed ranking.

dutch_arrival_defined_falsification.conclusion: The preregistered positive condition-dependent longer-window / post-arrival waiting mechanism is unsupported.

selection_diagnostic.interpretation: Measured condition-dependent activation selection does not explain the post-activation condition-speed pattern.

multivariate_entry_state_score.training: activation only: 0.756 x ordinal Durif + 0.379 x capture condition
multivariate_entry_state_score.interpretation: The capture-state vector that predicts entry and onset does not transfer as a general post-activation progression-speed ranking.
multivariate_entry_state_score.boundary: Activation-trained score is post hoc and shares individuals with transfer endpoints; post-activation analyses condition on activation.
